h1: HubSpot phone integration, with your calls on the record.
lede: A HubSpot phone integration connects your business phone system to HubSpot, so calls are placed from the CRM, logged to the contact record and stored with the recording attached. Stacktik, a RevOps (revenue operations) consultancy in Woodbridge, Ontario, helps you choose the phone system, connects it to HubSpot and tests it with your team, for a fixed fee quoted in writing.

summary.label: What it is
summary.text: Connecting a business phone system to HubSpot so calls are placed from the CRM and logged to the record with the recording.

summary.label: Who it is for

blocks.h2: HubSpot calling and the phone systems that connect to it.
blocks.intro: There is more than one way to get calls into HubSpot. The right one depends on how many people call, how calls are shared and what you already own. The proposal shortlists two or three with the monthly cost of each.

items.title: HubSpot's own calling
items.body: HubSpot includes calling from the record, with calling minutes set by your HubSpot plan. Whether that is enough depends on how your team shares lines and how much it calls, so we check it first.

items.title: Dialpad with HubSpot
items.body: Dialpad is one of the calling platforms in Stacktik's direct vendor programs. A Dialpad HubSpot integration puts calls and their recordings on the contact record.

items.title: CloudTalk with HubSpot
items.body: CloudTalk is another of our direct platforms. A CloudTalk HubSpot integration suits teams that call across countries and want each call logged in the CRM.

items.title: Kixie with HubSpot
items.body: Kixie is built for sales teams that dial in volume. Connected to HubSpot, each call and its outcome land on the record.

items.title: RingCentral, Aircall and Zoom
items.body: These come through our supplier network on the same proposal. HubSpot's Zoom integration covers meetings and webinars. Zoom Phone has a separate HubSpot app, so if you use Zoom for calls we check what that app logs first.

blocks.h2: What to decide before a HubSpot VoIP integration.
blocks.intro: An integration is only as good as the decisions made before it is switched on. These are the ones we settle in writing first, whoever you hire to connect the two.

items.title: Which users and numbers
items.body: Decide who is connected and which numbers are included. Shared lines and personal lines usually need different rules.

items.title: What gets logged
items.body: Every call, or only calls with a known contact. Logging everything is complete but noisy. Logging selectively is cleaner but can hide activity.

items.title: Who owns an unknown caller
items.body: When a number matches no record, decide whether a new contact is created, who owns it, and how a duplicate is avoided.

items.title: Where recordings and notes go
items.body: Whether the recording, the notes and the outcome are written to the contact, the deal or both, and who is allowed to listen.

items.title: What else depends on the call
items.body: Lead routing, follow-up tasks and the revenue scoreboard often read from call activity. We check each one still works after the phone system is connected.

blocks.h2: How Stacktik sets up a HubSpot phone integration.
blocks.intro: One technical RevOps consultant is assigned to your project and stays with it. The steps and their order are written on the proposal. This is the usual outline.

items.title: A free call
items.body: We go through how leads, calls and follow-ups move through your team today, what you use, and what isn't working. You get a straight answer on the right next step. No obligation.

items.title: A written proposal
items.body: Two or three phone options that fit how you call, each with its monthly cost, and our fixed fee for the setup. Keeping the phone system you have is one of the options where it connects to HubSpot.

items.title: The purchase, if you want it
items.body: Where it helps, we set the plan, seats and numbers up through the vendor's program, in your name. You can also buy direct.

items.title: Connect and test
items.body: The phone system is connected to HubSpot in your own accounts. We place test calls for each case you care about and check what lands on the record.

items.title: Training and handover
items.body: Training sessions on your own data, recorded for the team. Handover notes say how each piece runs and who to call. Ongoing support is optional and monthly.

faq.q: What is a HubSpot phone integration?
faq.a: A HubSpot phone integration connects a business phone system to HubSpot. Reps place calls from the contact record, and calls are logged there with the recording and outcome. It is also called a HubSpot VoIP integration or a VoIP CRM integration.

faq.q: Which phone system works best with HubSpot?
faq.a: It depends on how your team calls. HubSpot's own calling can be enough where your plan's calling limits fit. Dialpad, CloudTalk and Kixie suit teams that need shared lines, call queues or volume dialling. Stacktik shortlists two or three on a written proposal with the monthly cost of each.

faq.q: Is there a Dialpad HubSpot integration?
faq.a: Yes. Dialpad connects to HubSpot so calls are logged on the contact record. Dialpad is one of the calling platforms in Stacktik's direct vendor programs, and we set up the connection, the logging rules and the training.

Yes. HubSpot's Zoom integration covers meetings and webinars, and Zoom Phone has a separate HubSpot app for calls. If you want Zoom to carry your phone calls, Stacktik checks what that app writes to the HubSpot record before recommending it, and says so on the proposal.

faq.q: How much does a HubSpot phone integration cost?
faq.a: Stacktik quotes the setup as a fixed fee in writing before work starts. The phone system stays on its vendor's own plan and pricing, and the proposal shows that monthly cost beside each option. Nothing is charged for the first call.

faq.q: Do we have to change our phone system?
faq.a: No. If your current phone system connects well to HubSpot, we keep it and set up the integration. The proposal only recommends a change when it can be justified in writing.
